requirement: Parse an Authorization header as a case-insensitive Bearer scheme with exactly one token, verify the JWT for an audience, and report every failure as a 401 with a specific detail.
skeleton: AuthError with status and detail, extract_bearer checking presence, scheme and token shape, and authenticate decoding with a pinned algorithm and audience and wrapping JWT errors.
caption: Bearer token authentication with PyJWT. AuthError is an Exception carrying an HTTP status and a detail string. extract_bearer(header) raises AuthError 401 missing authorization header when the header is None, strips it and partitions on the first space, raises AuthError 401 saying the scheme must be Bearer unless the scheme matches bearer case-insensitively, then strips the rest and raises AuthError 401 malformed bearer token when it is empty or still contains a space. authenticate(header, secret, audience) extracts the token and decodes it with algorithms pinned to HS256 and the given audience; any jwt.InvalidTokenError, such as a bad signature or a wrong aud, is re-raised as AuthError 401 invalid token chained from the original. The fixture asserts that a valid header returns exactly sub alice and aud orders, that lowercase bearer and extra spaces are accepted, that None gives 401 missing authorization header, that a Basic header gives 401 with the scheme message, that Bearer a b and a bare Bearer give 401 malformed bearer token, and that a foreign signature or the billing audience gives 401 invalid token.

plan.intent: Authenticate requests from their Authorization header
constraints: A missing header raises AuthError 401 missing authorization header
The scheme is matched case-insensitively and other schemes raise AuthError 401
Empty tokens or tokens with spaces raise AuthError 401 malformed bearer token
Any jwt.InvalidTokenError becomes AuthError 401 invalid token
The audience and HS256 algorithm are enforced

rationale.teaches: Parse the header strictly but by the RFC, then convert the whole jwt.InvalidTokenError family into one 401 so no JWT exception leaks as a 500.
rationale.why: Catching only expiry lets forged tokens crash the handler, and a case-sensitive scheme check locks out standards-compliant clients.

ops.docstring: Pull a JWT out of an Authorization header and turn every failure into a 401.

candidates.why_wrong: The scheme comparison is case-sensitive, so lowercase bearer headers are refused.
A token with an embedded space reaches the decoder instead of being reported as malformed.
Only expiry is caught, so bad signatures and audiences escape as raw JWT errors.
A missing header is treated as an empty one and reported with the scheme message.
Invalid tokens answer 403, which claims the caller is known but forbidden.
